correctness.rationale: Since every antichain lies in one block, the polar factors into Q_m=Δ_m−Δ_m, where Δ_m is the simplex on 0 and the coordinate unit vectors. The candidates are 0, signed units and ordered differences. The origin is interior; a signed unit is exposed by a same-sign functional with a unique largest absolute coordinate, and e_a−e_b is exposed by the functional with 1 at a, −1 at b and 0 elsewhere. Thus the list of norms and vertices is exact. All product normals have squared norm at most H, and a pair of opposite farthest normals bounds every possible radius by 1/√H; the origin attains it. At this radius all farthest normals annihilate the center. Comparing normals that differ only by opposite singleton signs or opposite ordered differences gives exactly the indicated zero and block-constant coordinates. If j wide blocks use units, the worst dot product for that subset is the sum of the corresponding |t_i|. Its slack threshold f(j)=1−√(1−j/H) satisfies f(j)>j f(1) for j≥2 by strict convexity, with equality for j=0,1. Thus precisely the singleton bounds determine the center locus; exactly one-unit normals with matching signs can add contacts at an active coordinate. The product choices give both exact counts, and block indicators have mutually orthogonal lengths √m_i. With w=0 only the origin remains and all 2^s farthest facets touch it, including the interval k=m_1=1. These arguments are a universal verification from the polar inequalities in RESULT.md Steps 1–5. The reported 27 profiles, 7,210 test vertices and 121 corner counts were inspected in VERIFICATION.md and verification.py, not rerun. The separate reported 13-profile LP evidence was not needed or independently replayed.

evidence: Taking the largest Euclidean norm in the known polar list gives 1/√H and enumerating its maximizers gives F_0. These are not separately novel.

At radius 1/√H, identifying which translated centers attain equality requires analyzing all subsets of wide blocks. The strict inequality f(j)>j f(1) for j≥2 rules out both hidden constraints and additional boundary contacts.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The known facet lists do not directly state the optimal-center box or reduce the translated feasibility and contact equations to one-wide-block inequalities. The latter analysis is the useful distinct result.

evidence: The body is the orthogonal free sum of antipodally symmetrized cube hulls. Its block polars are simplex differences; a type-A root polytope identification by deleting the redundant coordinate changes the metric.

The distinct indexed box-Cayley criterion uses a projected simplex and separate fiber constraints. Central symmetry of such a Cayley polytope would force the projected simplex to be a segment; its fibers with common lower endpoints would then have constant widths. Thus it does not identify the present general centrally symmetric family.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Neither the metric-changing root representation nor a box locus for a different family transfers the optimal centers in this specified metric.

value.rationale: The exact set of translated maximum-radius balls is a natural refinement of a single centered radius in canonical Euclidean coordinates. It has unbounded dimension across the family, edge lengths that retain the actual block sizes, and a complete active-coordinate rule for contact counts on every face. These distinctions are not captured by total face counts or the centered insphere alone.
